skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

version.changelog:
Initial release of workplace group stress heatmap analysis skill.

- Provides anonymous, group-level stress heatmap analysis for open-plan office areas using fixed camera video.
- Detects facial tension and posture rigidity signals (e.g., frowning, rigid sitting, frequent eye rubbing) to compute a real-time stress index for each workstation zone.
- Generates color-coded stress heatmaps (green to red) and management suggestions without identifying individuals.
- Periodically outputs reports for organizational health monitoring; includes strong privacy measures (no personal identification).
- Integrates with enterprise security or health platforms as a smart-office feature.

llm.summary: This skill needs review because it promises anonymous group heatmaps but sends workplace video to a remote service while using personal identifiers and storing access tokens.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is anonymous, zone-level workplace stress heatmaps, but included code and docs expose broader generic video analysis, history lookup, device/record CRUD methods, and a bundled analysis API document with individual face/health-style diagnosis fields.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions require an open-id and may ask for a username or phone number, auto-trigger analysis/history queries, and do not consistently require an explicit privacy or authorization confirmation before employee video is analyzed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution or package-install hook was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages. A static scan warning for a raw private-IP dev configuration is downgraded because the default config points to production services, but it remains an environment hygiene issue.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Processing office camera footage for stress, fatigue, facial tension, and posture signals is highly sensitive; remote upload and arbitrary video URL ingestion are only partially disclosed and are not tightly scoped to approved enterprise camera sources.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The shared request layer can auto-create or log into an external account, attach user and tenant metadata to requests, and persist tokens/open tokens in a local SQLite user table with runtime schema mutation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only after confirming your organization has authority, employee notice/consent, retention rules, and a ban on individual discipline or performance use. Use an opaque service identifier instead of a phone number or personal username, verify where videos and reports are stored, and avoid submitting public or unauthorized camera URLs.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: requiring username/phone/open-id and attaching identity metadata conflicts with the artifact's repeated anonymous, group-only claims.
[SDI-1] expected: Partially accepted: cloud video analysis and report history fit an API-backed reporting skill, but user-linked history lookup, local token persistence, and broad URL ingestion are under-scoped for the stated privacy model.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the bundled smyx_analysis API documentation describes individualized face and health-style diagnosis outputs, which do not match anonymous workplace heatmap output.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact involves employee surveillance and inferred stress/health-like signals but lacks a strong mandatory consent, legal-basis, retention, and non-disciplinary-use gate in the execution flow.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: broad automatic triggers for uploaded office video and history-query keywords can initiate sensitive analysis or cloud lookups without enough explicit user control.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: Downgraded: the raw private-IP endpoint appears in a dev config, while the default config uses production URLs; this is not the main reason for review.
